safetyNote: Deadly poisonous. If ingestion is suspected, seek emergency medical or poison-centre advice immediately, even before symptoms appear; they are often delayed for at least six hours. Cooking does not make this mushroom safe.

sections.title: Death cap
sections.text: Amanita phalloides is a deadly ectomycorrhizal mushroom. Its cap is often olive or yellow-green with subtle radial fibres and a paler edge, but it can also be pale brown or nearly white. The cap expands from rounded to convex and then nearly flat; its margin is usually smooth rather than grooved.

sections.title: Gills, ring and volva
sections.text: The crowded gills and spore print are white. The gills are usually free from the stem, sometimes very narrowly attached. A thin, skirt-like membranous ring hangs high on the whitish stem; it may disappear with age or damage. The widened basal bulb sits in a loose, white, sac-like volva, which can remain hidden in the soil. Examine the whole base: a broken-off specimen can lose this crucial feature.

sections.title: Habitat and lookalikes
sections.text: In Europe it grows on the ground with broadleaved trees, especially oaks; it also occurs with other hosts and has spread with planted trees to other regions. Season varies by climate, often late summer to autumn in Europe. Young fruit bodies enclosed in the universal veil can resemble puffballs, but a lengthwise cut shows the developing cap, gills and stem. Colour or a single visible character cannot establish safe identification.

sections.title: Poisoning
sections.text: Amatoxins survive cooking and freezing and can cause severe liver injury. A silent period usually precedes vomiting, abdominal cramps and profuse diarrhoea; apparent improvement can be followed by liver failure. The amount required for severe poisoning varies, so no portion should be considered safe. If ingestion is possible, contact emergency medical services or a poison centre promptly and keep any remaining mushroom material for identification.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The plate shows a mature whole mushroom with its basal volva exposed, a longitudinal section, a cap top view and a white-gilled underside. It illustrates typical structures, not the full range of colour and age-related variation.
